diagnosis.root_cause: The router has never reported a heartbeat to monitoring: last_checkin is null and heartbeat_status is "never". This indicates a router reachability or monitoring-registration problem, although the subscriber's EPON link and service traffic are currently healthy.
evidence: The ONU is online and responding, with RX power -21.9 dBm in the normal band and TX power 2.34 dBm in the normal range.
The seven-day RX series is stable around -22 dBm, while TX power and TX bias remain stable; there is no fibre or laser degradation.
Distance is constant at 87, so there is no distance or path-change fault.
All tested peers on EPON0/4 are online and healthy, ruling out an ONU, splitter, PON-port, or shared OLT fault.
The OLT responds to ping and SNMP, and its CPU, memory, temperature, and uptime are healthy.
The VLAN is correctly provisioned as 1124, the RADIUS entry is present and CRM-consistent, and there are only three sessions in 24 hours with normal durations.
Traffic is active and stable, confirming that subscriber service is currently passing.

The only abnormal current state is the router heartbeat: last_checkin is null and heartbeat_status is "never". Per the calibrated rule, this means no heartbeat record has ever been received and requires router reachability or monitoring-registration investigation.

remediation.action: Verify router management reachability from the monitoring system, confirm the router is correctly registered and configured to send heartbeat/check-in data, and inspect management ACLs, routing, and monitoring credentials. Do not alter the EPON path or OLT configuration; customer service is currently passing normally. Re-run the router probe after correcting monitoring or management access.

ground_truth.root_cause: The router has no check-in record of any kind, which means it was never enrolled in heartbeat monitoring rather than that it stopped responding. Its customers are authenticated, holding long sessions and passing normal traffic.
expected_reasoning: The router's heartbeat status is 'never' with a null last_checkin
That is different from a heartbeat that went stale, which would carry a timestamp and an elapsed time
No record at all indicates the router was never enrolled in the check-in mechanism
The ONU behind it is online with RX -21.9 and TX 2.3, both normal
The live probe confirms the ONU and its peers are all responding normally
Sessions are active with a 683 minute mean, close to the 11.9 hour network norm
Daily traffic is steady across all seven days with no interruption
Customers on this router are being served, so there is no outage
The finding is a monitoring gap, not a network fault

expected_escalation.review_reason: Router is not enrolled in heartbeat monitoring and should be added

distractors: A null heartbeat looks worse than a stale one and invites a Disaster conclusion
A scheduled scan targeting the router frames it as the suspect
The correct answer is that nothing is wrong with the network
